title: Public art gallery funding and police surplus sharing
subtitle: Committee also received the Q3 2023 plan and financial update and a police surplus report.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that public art galleries again be eligible for regional operating support through Council-approved grant programs from January 1, 2024 {{vote:m2}}. Galleries have been excluded for 23 years, since a 2000 decision made them an area municipal responsibility. The recommendation settles eligibility only. How much funding is available will be considered at the November 29 budget meeting, with final approval planned for December 13.

The committee defeated a motion to split future Waterloo Region Police Service operating surpluses, with half kept in police reserves and half returned to the Region {{vote:m3}}. Under current practice, police keep the whole surplus and put it into their reserves. The committee also received for information a staff report on police surpluses and the Q3 2023 plan and financial update. Staff projected a regional surplus of about 0.8% of the tax levy, mainly from higher transit fare revenue.
Committee recommendations go to Regional Council for a final decision.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended reinstating public art galleries as eligible for regional operating support through Council-approved grant programs effective January 1, 2024 {{vote:m2}}.
The committee defeated a notice of motion to keep 50% of future police surpluses in police reserves and return 50% to the Region {{vote:m3}}.

debate: Supporters of the surplus motion said other regional departments keep no surpluses, and that returning half could ease budget pressure. They noted the Region already levies about $7 million a year for police reserves, so a share of an unplanned surplus would not destabilize operations.

Opponents said police reserves serve real purposes, including capital, development charges and long-term liabilities, and that some are projected to run in deficit within a year or two. They said the police budget has been prepared responsibly and that the Region's relationship with police is closely integrated.

Staff said municipalities treat police surpluses differently. Neither the Municipal Act nor the Police Services Act addresses them. The solicitor said police are co-governed with their board and are not a regional department in the usual sense.

One councillor warned the motion could lead to a confrontation with the Police Services Board, possibly ending before a tribunal. That councillor asked to wait until the police chief appears on November 22. Another asked why the chief was not at this meeting to explain the impact.
On the galleries, a councillor asked whether the funding envelope would grow. Staff said the preliminary budget keeps last year's figure and Council would decide the envelope later.
